# Documents warn you when they may be out of date

This feature flags parts of your documentation when the code they describe has changed since they were last written or checked. It works for architecture decisions, decisions recorded against a task, and sections of your living documents that are tied to specific files, so you always know where your documentation might need a second look.

## Contents

- [What it does for you](#what-it-does-for-you)
- [How it works](#how-it-works)
- [Good to know](#good-to-know)
- [Words used here](#words-used-here)

## What it does for you

- Shows a warning directly on the document or task where a part may be out of date
- Gives you a single checklist item that counts how many parts are possibly stale
- Lets you ask for a check against the code, or mark something as reviewed, one at a time or all at once
- Clears the warning automatically once a part is edited or confirmed as reviewed
- Also passes this warning along when an AI assistant is reading your documents, so it knows to double check before relying on them

## How it works

1. You link a document section, a decision, or an architecture decision to the relevant files in your project.
2. When code in those files changes, the system notices on its own, without needing anyone to run a check.
3. The affected part gets a warning shown wherever you view it.
4. You can review the checklist item showing how many parts are possibly stale.
5. You either fix the documentation, or mark the part as reviewed if it is still accurate.
6. The warning disappears until that code changes again.

## Good to know

- Changes to things like version numbers, changelogs, or test files do not trigger this warning, since they are not considered part of the actual logic.
- This check only looks at whether files changed, not whether the meaning of the documentation is still correct.

## Words used here

- ADR: a record of a decision about how the system is built or structured.
- Task: a unit of work, usually matching an issue or ticket, that documentation and decisions can be linked to.
- Section: one part of a living document, such as one topic in a glossary or design guide.
